answer: Defense in depth: Multiple layers of security controls (physical, network, host, application, data). Zero Trust: Never trust, always verify. Least privilege: Minimum access needed. Defense in depth: Multiple security controls.

Disable unused services and ports. Change default passwords and credentials. Disable unnecessary accounts. Enable encryption (WPA3, SSH). Apply patches and updates. Configure firewalls and ACLs. Implement network segmentation.

Packet Filtering: Examines headers, stateless. Stateful: Tracks connection state. Next-Generation Firewall (NGFW): Application-layer inspection, IDS/IPS integrated, SSL decryption. Proxy: Application-level gateway.

Filter traffic based on source/destination IP, port, protocol. Standard ACLs: Filter by source IP only (placed close to destination). Extended ACLs: Filter by source/dest/port (placed close to source). Applied inbound or outbound on interfaces.

Creates encrypted tunnel over public network. Site-to-site: Connects two networks (IPsec). Remote access: Individual users connect (SSL VPN, IPsec client). Protocols: IPsec (tunnel mode), TLS/SSL, L2TP, PPTP (deprecated).

Encrypts/authenticates IP packets. Two modes: Transport mode (only payload) and Tunnel mode (entire packet). Components: AH (Authentication Header), ESP (Encapsulating Security Payload), IKE (Internet Key Exchange).

Secure Socket Layer (deprecated) → Transport Layer Security. Encrypts data in transit. Uses certificates for authentication. Handshake: ClientHello, ServerHello, key exchange, encrypted communication. Port 443.

Port-based network access control. Authenticates devices before granting network access. Components: Supplicant (client), Authenticator (switch/AP), Authentication Server (RADIUS). Uses EAP (Extensible Authentication Protocol).

AAA protocol for network access. Authentication, Authorization, and Accounting. Uses UDP ports 1812 (auth) and 1813 (accounting). Centralized credential storage. Supports EAP for wireless authentication.

prompt: TACACS+ (Terminal Access Controller Access-Control System Plus)
answer: Cisco AAA protocol. Separates authentication, authorization, and accounting. Uses TCP port 49. Encrypts entire packet body (vs RADIUS encrypts only password). Better for command-level authorization.

Divides network into isolated segments (VLANs, subnets, zones). Limits lateral movement of threats. DMZ (Demilitarized Zone): Public-facing services isolated from internal network. Micro-segmentation: Per-workload security.

Isolated network segment between internal network and untrusted external network. Contains public-facing services (web servers, mail servers, DNS). Double firewall: External firewall protects DMZ, internal firewall protects DMZ from LAN.

Hides internal IP addresses from external networks. Provides a level of obscurity (not true security). PAT hides multiple internal addresses behind one public IP. Does not replace firewall protection.

IDS: Passive monitoring, alerts on suspicious activity (signature-based and anomaly-based). IPS: Active blocking, drops malicious packets. NIDS (Network-based) vs HIDS (Host-based). Can be signature or behavior-based.

SSH (port 22): Secure remote access. HTTPS (port 443): Secure web browsing. TLS: Secures email (SMTPS, IMAPS) and other protocols. IPsec: VPN and site-to-site encryption. SNMPv3: Secure network management.
Authentication: Verifying identity (who are you?). Authorization: Granting permissions (what can you do?). Accounting: Tracking activities (what did you do?). Implemented via RADIUS or TACACS+.

Disable unused services/ports. Change default passwords. Enable encryption. Implement network segmentation. Configure firewalls/ACLs. Enable logging and monitoring. Apply patches regularly. Implement 802.1X.
Controls network access based on MAC addresses (whitelist/blacklist). Easily bypassed with MAC spoofing. Should not be sole security measure. Used as additional layer alongside 802.1X.

Switch port security limits MAC addresses per port. Violation actions: Shutdown, Restrict, Protect. Prevents unauthorized devices from connecting to network ports. Works with 802.1X for stronger security.

Prevents unauthorized data exfiltration. Inspects data in transit, at rest, and in use. Can block sensitive data transfers via email, web, or USB. Uses content inspection, context matching, and policy enforcement.
